segment: Segment 1: founder-led Indian software product, solo builder
industry: Developer and security tooling (network traffic interception)
size: 1 named builder; team size not stated
fit_reason: Paid desktop software ($200 per year) built by one named security engineer, office address in Bengaluru, public GitHub org with repos pushed this week, and a feature release (v2.1.0) published 2026-10-25 after v2.0.0 on 2026-10-04.

evidence.claim: Pricing: "$200 per year" with "Every protocol and feature, no tiers", a seven-day trial, and Windows, macOS and Linux builds. A paid software product.

The about page names one builder and no team: "Built by a security engineer, for security engineers." and "Sourav is a security engineer who spent years testing the full stack" (the page does not use the word founder; it names no legal entity).

Footer address: "235, Binnamangala, 2nd Floor, 13th Cross Road, 2nd Stage, Indira Nagar, Bengaluru - 560038"; terms "Last updated: October 31, 2026"; no country or governing law is stated on the page.

GitHub release v2.1.0 published_at 2026-10-25T09:59:26Z; release notes open with "New features" (traffic redirect on Windows, one-click CA install). The page does not call it major. v2.0.0 was published 2026-10-04T08:46:12Z, three days before the 30-day window.

Blog post "InterceptSuite 2.1.0: Built-in Traffic Redirect for Windows and One-Click CA Install" dated October 25, 2026; "InterceptSuite 2.0.0: Replay, Interception Rules, Scope and AI Access (MCP)" dated October 6, 2026.

GitHub org InterceptSuite: location "India", website interceptsuite.com, 88 followers; pinned repo ProxyBridge last updated Nov 5, 2026 and InterceptSuite last updated Oct 25, 2026. The org shows one public member, whose profile name matches the builder on the about page.
Two releases in three weeks (2.0.0 then 2.1.0), each with its own blog post, suggests recurring launch content. Our inference only; no stated need for launch video was found.

score_rationale: Software, Bengaluru, named solo builder and GitHub fit; team size, a dated major launch and any stated video need are missing, and the contact is a form, so tier C.
